title: US Warns EB-1 Green Cards May Run Out for Indians Before September Ends
excerpt: The State Department's September Visa Bulletin flags that surging demand could exhaust India's EB-1 allocation before the fiscal year closes on September 30, adding to an already dire backlog across employment-based categories.
body:
• The US State Department warns EB-1 green cards for Indians may become unavailable within weeks if India's annual allocation is exhausted before September 30.
  • India's EB-2 category is already listed as unavailable for September, while EB-3 has a 12-year backlog with a final action date of January 1, 2014.
  • The EB-1 India final action date is October 15, 2022 — only applicants with earlier priority dates are eligible for processing.
  • A statutory 7% per-country cap on employment-based visas forces Indian applicants into multi-decade queues despite outsized demand.

The US State Department has warned that employment-based first-preference (EB-1) green cards could become unavailable for Indian applicants within weeks, adding fresh uncertainty for high-skilled professionals who already face severe backlogs across nearly every immigration pathway.

The warning, published in the September 2026 Visa Bulletin, stated that "high demand and number use by aliens chargeable to India in the EB-1 visa category may necessitate making the category unavailable in the coming weeks if India's pro-rated limit in the EB-1 category is reached before the fiscal year ends."

What the Numbers Show

The EB-1 category covers priority workers: individuals with extraordinary ability, outstanding professors and researchers, and certain multinational executives and managers. It has historically been the fastest employment-based immigration pathway, making a potential closure especially consequential.

https://x.com/moneycontrolcom/status/2097244801452347394

For September, the EB-1 India final action date stands at October 15, 2022. An Indian applicant must generally hold a priority date earlier than that cutoff for a visa number to be available for final processing. The dates-for-filing chart — which governs when applicants can submit adjustment-of-status applications — lists December 1, 2023, for EB-1 India, offering somewhat more room, though applicants must verify which chart USCIS authorizes each month.

A Backlog Across Every Category

The EB-1 warning comes against an already dire landscape. India's EB-2 category, covering professionals with advanced degrees and those of exceptional ability, is listed as "U" — unavailable — for September, continuing its status from August. No visa numbers are being issued in that category.

The EB-3 India final action date is January 1, 2014, a queue stretching back more than 12 years. For comparison, the EB-3 date for most other countries is September 1, 2024, meaning applicants from India wait roughly a decade longer than their peers. India's unreserved EB-5 investor category is also unavailable for final action in September.

"High demand and number use by aliens chargeable to India in the EB-1 visa category may necessitate making the category unavailable in the coming weeks."

— US State Department, September 2026 Visa Bulletin

Why Indian Applicants Face Steeper Odds

The structural driver is a statutory 7% per-country cap on employment-based and family-sponsored preference visas. For fiscal year 2026, the worldwide employment-based preference limit is set at 186,317 visas. Because India generates a disproportionately large share of high-skilled immigration petitions — particularly in technology, research, and management — it consistently hits the per-country ceiling before other nations.

This year's warning echoes what happened in fiscal year 2025. Last September, the EB-1 category reached its annual limit on September 8, 2025, followed by EB-3 the next day, after EB-2 had already been exhausted on September 2, according to immigration law firm Foster Global. All employment-based categories were shut for the final weeks of that fiscal year.

What Applicants Should Do

If the EB-1 category closes before September 30, affected Indian applicants would need to wait until the new fiscal year opens on October 1 for fresh visa numbers. USCIS would continue accepting applications during a closure period, but could not approve them until new numbers become available.

Immigration attorneys recommend that applicants with pending EB-1 cases monitor official Visa Bulletin updates and USCIS instructions closely rather than relying on unofficial predictions. The State Department has said it will make adjustments as needed based on rolling demand data.

The Bigger Picture

The potential EB-1 closure underscores a broader crisis in the US immigration system for Indian nationals. With EB-2 already shut, EB-3 backed up 12 years, and EB-1 now at risk, Indian professionals face a narrowing set of options for permanent residency. Advocacy groups tracking the backlog are expected to press for legislative relief, though no statutory change addressing per-country caps is currently before Congress.
